name: How Do You Compare Two Kitchen Remodel Estimates With Different Allowances?

mainEntity.name: How can I compare two kitchen remodeling estimates when the cabinet, countertop, and fixture allowances are different?
mainEntity.text: How can I compare two kitchen remodeling estimates when the cabinet, countertop, and fixture allowances are different?

acceptedAnswer.text: Different allowances make two kitchen estimates appear comparable when they are not. Start by listing every allowance in a comparison sheet: cabinets, countertops, sinks, faucets, lighting, appliances, hardware, flooring, and backsplash. Record the dollar amount, quantity, measurement, product grade, installation coverage, delivery, tax, and whether unused funds are credited. Ask each contractor to revise the proposal using the same selections or realistic local prices. For example, compare semi-custom cabinets with semi-custom cabinets rather than placing a stock-cabinet allowance beside a custom-cabinet allowance. Do the same for quartz thickness, edge treatment, backsplash tile, sink type, and faucet quality. Confirm whether cabinet hardware, fillers, panels, trim, and finishing pieces are included because these details can materially change the final price. Calculate the difference between the allowance and your expected purchase price. Ask whether the contractor adds markup, handling fees, or labor when an allowance is exceeded, and whether credits apply when you spend less. Keep written records of every selection and approval. The most useful comparison is the expected completed price, not the lowest starting total.
acceptedAnswer.description: Convert each allowance into comparable quantities and product standards before comparing totals. Ask contractors to price the same cabinet construction, countertop material, hardware, fixtures, and installation. A lower allowance may reduce the initial estimate but create a larger balance when actual selections cost more.
